# Second-Life EV Batteries: Research Synthesis

## Scale and Remaining Capacity

Second-life EV batteries currently make up under 3% of global deployed energy storage capacity. More than 120 GWh of EV batteries are expected to reach end-of-vehicle life in 2026, and over half of that volume will still have 70-80% usable capacity. [Source: https://recharged.com/articles/second-life-ev-batteries-explained] (confidence: medium; the finding gives no page number, because it comes from a web page.)

## Pilot Results

Second-life battery pilots, which repurpose retired EV battery packs for stationary storage, are running at two sites. Early results show retained capacity of 70-78% after automotive service life. [Source: sample-report.md, page 3] (confidence: high)

## Cross-Source Consistency

The pilot figure of 70-78% retained capacity (sample-report.md, page 3) sits inside the 70-80% range that the web source gives for batteries reaching end of vehicle life (https://recharged.com/articles/second-life-ev-batteries-explained). The pilot report itself describes its results as in line with third-party estimates (sample-report.md, page 3). This is my comparison of the two findings. Neither source states it.

## Caveats

- The web finding has medium confidence and comes from a single article. No page number was provided, so a page-level citation is not possible.
- The pilot data covers only two sites and is described as early results (sample-report.md, page 3). It should not be generalised to the wider market.
- The findings contain nothing on economics, safety, degradation over the second life, or the identity of the pilot sites, so this report does not address those topics.

## What Are Second-Life EV Batteries?

Second-life EV batteries are used EV packs that no longer meet automaker standards for in-vehicle range or performance, but still have enough capacity and health to be safely reused in lower-stress applications like stationary energy storage.

## Current Market Scale in 2026

In 2026, more than 120 GWh of EV batteries worldwide will reach end-of-vehicle life, but over half of those packs will still have 70-80% usable capacity. However, second-life EV batteries currently represent under 3% of global deployed energy storage capacity.

## Market Developments

Moment Energy has officially opened what it says is the world's largest second-life EV battery factory, bringing new battery energy storage manufacturing capacity online just six weeks after announcing the project. Additionally, in June 2026, B2U and Waymo announced a partnership to route batteries from Waymo's autonomous vehicle fleet into grid storage.

## Economic Outlook

New LFP cell prices have fallen below US$100/kWh as of mid-2026, directly compressing the cost advantage second-life batteries depend on to cover diagnostics, repackaging, and elevated operations and maintenance costs. Second-life storage is structurally sound with a genuine growth trajectory, but its mainstream moment is a 2030s story, not a 2026-2028 one.

## Environmental Benefits

Second-life applications of EV batteries can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 22%-51% in residential energy storage and 7%-31% in utility applications.
